summary: Learn to govern humanitarian and social protection data, sharing, interoperability, privacy, and AI risks. Build practical artefacts in this five-day course.
lede: Data and AI governance in humanitarian and social protection settings provides a structured approach to responsible information use across organisations. It is for professionals coordinating programme, monitoring, information, or policy data who need to manage shared data and analytics responsibly. Participants practise mapping information flows, assessing privacy and AI risks, and establishing oversight and accountability processes.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals coordinating humanitarian data, social protection information, MEAL evidence, and responsible analytics across organisational boundaries. It suits intermediate practitioners who already work with programme, monitoring, information, or policy data and need a structured governance approach.
prerequisites: You should have working experience in humanitarian programmes, social protection delivery, MEAL, information management, digital transformation, data analysis, or related policy work. No programming background is required, and the exercises focus on governance artefacts, structured analysis, spreadsheets, and dashboard interpretation rather than model coding. Bring a current data-sharing, analytics, MEAL, or digital transformation challenge if organisational confidentiality permits; otherwise, provided scenarios and datasets will support the practical work.
